title: KML Coordinate Block Counter: Geometry Census
description: Count the coordinates elements in a KML file with the KML Coordinate Block Counter — blocks per geometry type, counted locally. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a boundary KML with 3 Polygons, 2 LineStrings and 8 Points holds 14 coordinate blocks — one per geometry part — a structural census this counter reads in seconds.
quick_answer: The KML Coordinate Block Counter counts the <coordinates> elements in a KML file — one block per Point, LineString, LinearRing or other geometry part — and reports the structural total. Drop the file and read how its geometry is organised, locally, before importing it anywhere.

body.t: Blocks, not placemarks, reveal complexity: a single Placemark with a MultiGeometry can hold dozens. Compare with the
to see features versus geometry parts.
Every block is a draw call's worth of geometry; hundreds of blocks warn of heavy files before the map slows down to tell you.
An export that split one polygon into 40 blocks used a different geometry model than expected — the count exposes the modelling choice.
Blocks with zero or one tuples are degenerate geometry that importers choke on. The census is the early warning.
One LineString block can hold 900 coordinate tuples (lon,lat pairs) in a single <coordinates> element. This counter counts the block as 1. For tuple-level counting, the geometry's own length tools (

A Polygon with a hole has 2 blocks: the outer LinearRing and the inner ring. A 12-polygon boundary with 3 holes totals 12 + 3 = 15 ring/point blocks before any Point or LineString is counted — structure you can verify by hand.

popular_table.note: The count is structural: it tallies elements, not vertices. Both numbers matter; this page owns the element census.

faq: Does it count individual coordinate pairs?
No — it counts <coordinates> blocks. A block may hold one pair (a Point) or thousands (a detailed LineString). The distinction is the page's whole point, and the examples show how to read it.
Overlays position imagery with a LatLonBox, not a coordinates element — honestly excluded from this census, and listed as such in the table.
A KMZ is a zipped KML — unzip it (any archive tool) and count the doc.kml inside.
A <coordinates> element with no tuples is malformed but countable — the census includes it and the anomaly is worth your attention.
gx:Track stores <gx:coord> elements instead of <coordinates> — a Google extension namespace this standard census does not fold in.
MultiGeometries and holed polygons: geometry parts outnumber features whenever shapes get serious. The placemark counter gives the feature side of the ratio.
Placemarks can hold no geometry at all (a labelled folder entry, a camera view) — features without blocks are the mirror case.
